title: Job 37 — Elihu's storm hymn: the thunder, snow and lightning of El

verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: ʾap-lĕzōʾt yeḥĕrad libbî wĕyittar mimmĕqômô (Qal impf. ḥrd; ntr 'start up'). 'trembles, and leaps up from its place' is exact; no outer quotation marks, as job-woh 38-41.
šimʿû šāmôaʿ (impv. + inf. abs.) 'Hear, hear'; bĕrōgez qōlô 'the rumbling of his voice'; hegeh 'sound'. Exact; the Ugaritic thunder comparandum is kept out of the line.

taḥat-kol-haššāmayim yišrēhû (šrh 'let loose') / wĕʾôrô ʿal-kanpôt hāʾāreṣ. 'skies' is the physical sky; 'the wings of the land' reproduces the stable job-woh 38:13 phrase verbatim (checked), with ASV 'ends of the earth' recorded.
ʾaḥărāyw yišʾag-qôl yarʿēm bĕqôl gĕʾônô wĕlōʾ yĕʿaqqĕbēm: 'he does not hold them back' (Piel ʿqb) is the ASV sense. Exact.
yarʿēm ʾēl bĕqôlô niplāʾôt: niplāʾôt adverbial, 'wondrously'. Bare ʾēl 'El' matches the stable job-woh 38:41 and 40:9 (checked) under the extended shaddai-eloah.

kî laššeleg yōʾmar hĕwēʾ ʾāreṣ: hĕwēʾ is the Aramaizing impv. of hwh 'fall'; the embedded speech is marked with double quotes per the lineation convention. 'earth' for the ground the snow falls on is the ASV and the overlay scope rule.

bĕyad-kol-ʾādām yaḥtôm lādaʿat kol-ʾanšê maʿăśēhû: 'He seals up the hand of every human, that all the men of his making may know' keeps the MT construct (no supplied object); the revocalization is recorded. ʾādām 'human' matches job-woh 38:26.
wattābōʾ ḥayyâ bĕmô-ʾāreb ûbimʿônōteyhā tiškōn: 'the beast goes into its lair, and remains in its dens'. Exact.

min-haḥeder tābôʾ sûpâ ûmimmĕzārîm qārâ: the line correctly does not supply the ASV's 'of the south'; mĕzārîm 'the north' with the 'scatterers' sense in commentary. sûpâ 'storm' is the same English at Prov 10:25 (checked).

minnišmat-ʾēl yitten-qāraḥ wĕrōḥab mayim bĕmûṣāq: 'By the breath of El ice is given, and the breadth of the waters is constrained' (ASV 'straitened'); the NJPS 'cast metal' alternative is recorded. Exact.
ʾap-bĕrî yaṭrîaḥ ʿāb yāpîṣ ʿănan ʾôrô: rî 'moisture' (hapax), ʿāb 'thick cloud' and ʿānān 'cloud' kept apart from šĕḥāqîm. Exact.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: Source checked: Ketiv בתחבולתו, Qere בְּתַחְבּוּלֹתָיו; Qere translated ('by his guidance', ASV) with the number difference recorded. ʿal-pĕnê tēbēl ʾārĕṣâ 'over the face of the inhabited world, on the earth' is exact.

ʾim-lĕšēbeṭ ʾim-lĕʾarṣô ʾim-lĕḥesed yamṣiʾēhû: MT lĕʾarṣô 'for his land' kept with the emendation recorded. Solitary ḥesed 'kindness' applies central chesed-solitary (founder point E; the rendering is lexically sound).
haʾăzînâ zōʾt ʾiyyôb ʿămōd wĕhitbônēn niplĕʾôt ʾēl: 'Job' as in all stable job-woh chapters; 'El'. Exact.
hătēdaʿ bĕśûm-ʾĕlôah ʿălêhem wĕhôpîaʿ ʾôr ʿănānô: 'how Eloah lays his charge upon them' (ASV) and 'makes the lightning of his cloud shine' (Hiphil ypʿ). Exact; 'Eloah' as job-woh 40:2.
mipleśê-ʿāb 'the balancings of the thick cloud' (hapax; ASV), miplĕʾôt tĕmîm dēʿîm. Exact; the cross-reference to 36:4 is accurate.
ʾăšer-bĕgādeykā ḥammîm bĕhašqiṭ ʾereṣ middārôm: 'when the earth is stilled by the south wind'. Exact.

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (FR 'des nuages, solides'; EN 'the sky, which is strong')
verdicts.reasoning: Line approved. Re-parsed tarqîaʿ ʿimmô lišḥāqîm ḥăzāqîm kirʾî mûṣāq: rqʿ 'beat out, spread out'; šĕḥāqîm 'clouds' is the lexical sense (BDB 'dust, cloud'; HALOT 'thin cloud', pl. 'clouds, sky'), the KJV/stable job-woh rendering of the word at 38:37, and keeps šĕḥāqîm apart from šāmayim 'skies' (37:3); ḥăzāqîm stays 'strong', not the canon's 'solides', so the line does not lean toward the reception. Revise (commentary only): the reception note quotes only the canon's French 'nuages'. The canon's English edition renders the verse 'hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong' (TBWTT-3:259 EN). Add one sentence: "The canon's English edition has 'the sky, which is strong'; the canon itself is therefore divided, and the line's 'clouds' follows the lexical entry, not either wording." This is the treatment already given at Prov 8:22 ('created' vs canon-EN 'possessed').
hôdîʿēnû mah-nnōʾmar lô lōʾ-naʿărōk mippĕnê-ḥōšek: ʿrk 'set in order' (also of a legal case). Exact.
hayĕsuppar-lô kî ʾădabbēr ʾim-ʾāmar ʾîš kî yĕbullāʿ: the ASV double-question structure is the literal parse; the conditional construal is recorded. Exact.

wĕʿattâ lōʾ rāʾû ʾôr bāhîr hûʾ baššĕḥāqîm wĕrûaḥ ʿābĕrâ wattĕṭahărēm: 'clouds' (new central entry) gives wattĕṭahărēm 'cleared them' its natural antecedent; rûaḥ 'wind'. ASV 'skies' recorded. Defensible and not canon-dependent (the canon does not cite this verse).
miṣṣāpôn zāhāb yeʾĕteh ʿal-ʾĕlôah nôrāʾ hôd: 'golden splendor' (ASV) with literal 'gold' and the Ṣapānu view in commentary. Exact.
šadday lōʾ-mĕṣāʾnuhû śaggîʾ-kōaḥ ûmišpāṭ wĕrōb-ṣĕdāqâ lōʾ yĕʿanneh: 'Shaddai' kept (central shaddai-eloah); the alternative division is recorded. Exact.
lākēn yĕrēʾûhû ʾănāšîm lōʾ-yirʾeh kol-ḥakmê-lēb: 'men fear him; he does not regard any who are wise of heart' (ASV). Petucha retained in the Hebrew. Exact.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Philologically neutral and correctly direct: a typographic convention, with the Hebrew form standing in the source text and every name verified (David, Solomon, Jerusalem, Zion, Israel, Jacob, Job). Flagged only because it is founder point D (the corpus split with the Kings transliteration). Reviewer view: accept English forms for the Writings. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, which are not retro-edited, and the four books must agree with each other. Record the genre split (narrative transliterated, poetry English) as deliberate, or settle it corpus-wide in one later decision.

Every site verified: YHWH; 'Yah' (Ps 147:1, 20); the article follows the Hebrew (anarthrous Ps 8:6; Eccl 3:10, 13; articular Eccl 3:11, 14, 15, 17, 18); 'El', 'Eloah' and 'Shaddai' as in stable job-woh (38:41; 40:2, 9); 'our Lord' for ʾădōnênû. Direct is right: these are presentation rules over explicit Hebrew forms. Flagged only for founder point A (Ps 8:6 'Elohim' against the canon's 'the Elohim'). Reviewer view: keep the anarthrous form. The Hebrew has no article, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and the Kings clause 2, and departing from the canon's wording here is evidence that the line is not canon-driven.

Site-by-site application of the founder's Kings-wave register ruling, checked verse by verse: physical sky 'skies' (Ps 8:2, 4, 9; 19:2, 7; 33:6; 147:8; Prov 8:27; Eccl 3:1; Job 37:3); dwelling or cosmic height 'heavens' (Ps 33:13 || mĕkôn-šibtô; 139:8 against She'ol). Ps 8:2 ('splendor upon the skies') is the closest call and is argued from v 4. Direct is appropriate.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

The lexical mapping is accurate and consistent with central ha-adam / ben-adam (direct) and with GEN-WOH-11:5 'the sons of the human' (checked). ʾĕnôš 'a mortal' and ʾîšîm 'O men' are sound. Flagged for founder point B. The articular/anarthrous split ('the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human', Prov 8:4, 31) is formally exact but yields stiff English, and in Biblical Hebrew the two forms are not distinct in sense. The corpus is now split three ways ('sons of men' ASV / canon-EN; 'children of men' 1 Kgs 8:39; 'sons of the human' Gen 11:5). Reviewer view: accept the editor's forms for coherence with the central entries, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 to them. If the founder prefers idiom, revert all bĕnê (hā)ʾādām sites together to 'the sons of men' with a string swap, and leave the singular ben-adam untouched.

Inferred is the honest class: the traditional English of Eccl 3:21 is 'spirit'. The lexical evidence is real. BDB and HALOT give rûaḥ 'breath (of life)'; NJPS has 'lifebreath' at Eccl 3:21; and vv 19-21 argue about the one rûaḥ that humans and beasts share (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22). Lower-case 'spirit' at Ps 139:7 follows NRSV and NJPS. 'wind' (Job 37:21; Ps 147:18) and 'breath of his mouth' (Ps 33:6) are uncontroversial.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012)
glossaryReview.reasoning: All six pairs were verified in the Leningrad source (Job 37:12; Ps 139:6, 16; 147:19; Prov 8:17, 35), and all Qere are translated. The ASV-follows-Ketiv statements at Ps 139:16 and 147:19 are correct. No seventh pair exists: Prov 8:16 is a manuscript variant, as the editor says. Direct is correct.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.

citations: Yeivin, Introduction to the Tiberian Masorah (1980), on the poetic accents
glossaryReview.reasoning: One line per Masoretic verse, divided at the main disjunctive; no outer quotation marks for Elihu or Wisdom (as stable job-woh 38-41); colon for Qohelet's internal speech (ASV). Verified across all nine chapters.

Approve the entry and the class direct. šaḥaq 'fine dust' / pl. 'clouds' (BDB, HALOT), KJV 'clouds' at Job 38:37 and Prov 3:20; 8:28, and the stable JOB-WOH-38:37 all support it. Two corrections are needed before it is applied. (1) The wohChoice pre-lists Ps 89:7, 38 under 'clouds' but then says 'singular šaḥaq "fine dust" (Isa 40:15)'. At Ps 89:7 and 89:38 the form is the singular baššaḥaq and means the sky or the clouds, not dust. Reword the clause: "singular šaḥaq is 'fine dust' at Isa 40:15; the singular baššaḥaq of Ps 89:7, 38 ('in the sky / clouds') is decided at those sites." Either drop 89:7, 38 from the pre-listed sites or keep them under that clause. (2) The rationale names only the canon's French ('nuages solides') at Job 37:18. Add that the canon's English edition renders the verse 'the sky, which is strong', so that the record shows the canon is divided and the entry does not depend on it.

Append-only (verified). It extends the stable job-woh practice for bare ʾēl ('El', 38:41; 40:9) to Job 37 and to Ps 19:2; 139:17, 23, and 'Eloah' to Ps 139:19, and it names the isaiah-woh 'God' exception explicitly. All appliesTo sites were checked against the Hebrew.
appliesTo +12 matches appliesToAdded exactly (verified against base); every site carries the ref and follows the register rule.
appliesTo +3 ('land' sites only: Job 37:3, 13; Prov 10:30), verified; the 'earth' sites are correctly left to the overlay.

+10 sites verified, including articular bĕnê hāʾādām on the GEN-WOH-11:5 precedent. If founder point B reverts the plurals, drop PSA-WOH-33:13 and ECC-WOH-3:10, 18, 19, 21 from this op and keep the singular sites.

citations: Sakenfeld, The Meaning of Hesed in the Hebrew Bible (1978)
glossaryReview.reasoning: The extension is correct and the changed lines were verified (Ps 33:5, 18, 22; 147:11; Job 37:13). 'kindness' is lexically defensible for solitary ḥesed (Glueck; Sakenfeld). Flagged for founder point E only, because the Psalter has about 120 further occurrences. Reviewer view: confirm 'kindness' now, before the Psalms grow, so that the rendering does not drift. It is the central wohChoice, it is consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and the loyalty sense is carried in commentary. 'steadfast love' (NRSV) is the main alternative.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: All 24 lines checked. Storm vocabulary keeps its meteorological sense (2-5, 9-11, 15-17, 21-22). The one canon-coincident line, 37:18 'clouds', rests on BDB/HALOT, the KJV and stable job-woh 38:37, and keeps ASV 'strong' instead of the canon's 'solides'. The 'metallic craft' reading is confined to a labelled reception note. No flags.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 205 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 16 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, the Leningrad source files, the overlays, the diff, the 2.83.0 base and the canon-quotation file before wave-w1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's list of the three canon-coincident lines (section 1) confirmed the two commentary revisions: at Job 37:18 and Prov 8:30 the notes cite only the canon's French, whose wording matches the line, and omit the canon's English ('the sky'; 'as one brought up with him'), which does not. Prov 8:22 already shows the correct treatment. The report's six-pair Ketiv/Qere count was independently confirmed.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-Ps-8:6-article-on-Elohim: Keep 'a little less than Elohim' without the article. The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. Differing from the canon here is useful evidence that the line follows the Hebrew.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-bene-(ha)adam: Accept 'the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human' for coherence with central ha-adam / ben-adam and GEN-WOH-11:5, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 ('the children of men') to it. The cost is stiff English at Prov 8:4, 31, and the Hebrew article on bĕnê (hā)ʾādām carries no difference in sense. If the founder prefers idiom, revert every plural site together to 'the sons of men' (string swap; drop the plural refIds from the ha-adam and ben-adam ops). Do not mix the two.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-eretz-cosmic-earth: Agree. Promote the 'earth' scope clause (isaiah-woh + Writings) to central eretz in a dedicated later diff, after the parallel appliesTo merges have landed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-proper-names: Accept English forms in the four Writings books. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, and the four books must agree. Record the corpus practice as genre-split (narrative transliterated, poetry and prophets English) or settle it in one corpus-wide decision. Do not leave it implicit.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-chesed-kindness: Confirm 'kindness' for solitary ḥesed now, before the Psalter grows (about 120 occurrences). It is the central wohChoice, consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and lexically sound (Glueck; Sakenfeld). The loyalty sense stays in commentary, and the fixed pair ḥesed wĕʾĕmet stays under chesed-v-emet.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-Job-37:18-clouds: No decision needed: 'clouds' rests on BDB/HALOT, KJV and stable job-woh 38:37, and 'strong' (not 'solid') keeps the line neutral. The reviewer asks for one transparency sentence (JOB-WOH-37:18 revise; shechaqim op revise): the canon's English edition reads 'the sky', so the canon is itself divided.

paragraphs.text: אַף־לְ֭זֹאת יֶחֱרַ֣ד לִבִּ֑י וְ֝יִתַּ֗ר מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: At this also my heart trembles, and leaps up from its place.

notes.official: Job 37 closes Elihu's fourth speech (36:1-37:24). As in job-woh 38-41, a speech that fills the chapter is printed without outer quotation marks, and embedded speech (v 6) takes double quotation marks (`poetic-lineation-and-speech-convention-writings`). *yeḥĕrad libbî wĕyittar mimmĕqômô* 'my heart trembles, and leaps up from its place' (*ntr* 'spring up, start').

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֣וֹעַ בְּרֹ֣גֶז קֹל֑וֹ וְ֝הֶ֗גֶה מִפִּ֥יו יֵצֵֽא׃

i18n.en: Hear, hear the rumbling of his voice, and the sound that goes out from his mouth.

notes.official: *šimʿû šāmôaʿ* 'Hear, hear': the infinitive absolute intensifies the imperative. *bĕrōgez qōlô* 'the rumbling of his voice': *rōgez* is agitation, turmoil (ASV 'noise'). *hegeh* 'sound, rumble'. The storm vocabulary of vv 2-5 keeps its meteorological sense throughout. The central Ugaritic thunder-voice entry (`qlh-qds-tr-arts-thunder-voice-theophany-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible-psalm-29`) cites these verses as a comparandum but governs the Baal Cycle lines only.

paragraphs.text: תַּֽחַת־כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֥יִם יִשְׁרֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אוֹר֗וֹ עַל־כַּנְפ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Under the whole of the skies he lets it loose, and his lightning to the wings of the land.

notes.official: *taḥat-kol-haššāmayim yišrēhû* 'Under the whole of the skies he lets it loose': the physical sky (central `shamayim`). *wĕʾôrô ʿal-kanpôt hāʾāreṣ* 'and his lightning to the wings of the land'. *ʾôr* 'light' is lightning here (ASV 'lightning'; also vv 11, 15). *kanpôt hāʾāreṣ* is rendered as in the stable job-woh 38:13, 'the wings of the land' (central `eretz`), the edges of the inhabited land (ASV 'the ends of the earth'; `eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: אַחֲרָ֤יו ׀ יִשְׁאַג־ק֗וֹל יַ֭רְעֵם בְּק֣וֹל גְּאוֹנ֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יְ֝עַקְּבֵ֗ם כִּֽי־יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹלֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: After it a voice roars; he thunders with the voice of his majesty, and he does not hold them back when his voice is heard.

notes.official: *yišʾag-qôl* 'a voice roars'; *yarʿēm bĕqôl gĕʾônô* 'he thunders with the voice of his majesty'; *wĕlōʾ yĕʿaqqĕbēm* 'he does not hold them back', the lightnings or the rains.

paragraphs.text: יַרְעֵ֤ם אֵ֣ל בְּ֭קוֹלוֹ נִפְלָא֑וֹת עֹשֶׂ֥ה גְ֝דֹל֗וֹת וְלֹ֣א נֵדָֽע׃

i18n.en: El thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things, and we do not know them.

notes.official: *yarʿēm ʾēl bĕqôlô niplāʾôt* 'El thunders wondrously with his voice'. Bare *ʾēl* is transliterated 'El', as in job-woh 38:41 and 40:9 (ASV 'God'); the central `shaddai-eloah` entry is extended in this wave to cover it (`divine-names-convention-writings`). The dialogues of the book use *ʾēl*, *ʾĕlôah* and *šadday*; YHWH belongs to the prose frame and the divine speeches.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י לַשֶּׁ֨לַג ׀ יֹאמַ֗ר הֱוֵ֫א אָ֥רֶץ וְגֶ֥שֶׁם מָטָ֑ר וְ֝גֶ֗שֶׁם מִטְר֥וֹת עֻזּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: For to the snow he says, "Fall to the earth"; likewise to the downpour of rain, and the downpour of his mighty rains.

notes.official: *kî laššeleg yōʾmar hĕwēʾ ʾāreṣ* 'For to the snow he says, "Fall to the earth"': *hĕwēʾ* is the imperative of *hwh* 'fall' (BDB), a rare, Aramaizing verb. *ʾereṣ* is the ground on which the snow falls, so 'earth' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`). *gešem māṭār ... gešem miṭrôt ʿuzzô* 'the downpour of rain, and the downpour of his mighty rains'.

paragraphs.text: בְּיַד־כָּל־אָדָ֥ם יַחְתּ֑וֹם לָ֝דַ֗עַת כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

i18n.en: He seals up the hand of every human, that all the men of his making may know.

notes.official: *bĕyad-kol-ʾādām yaḥtôm* 'He seals up the hand of every human': the storm stops human work (ASV 'sealeth up the hand of every man'). *ʾādām* is 'human', as at job-woh 38:26 (central `ha-adam`; `adam-enosh-ish-human-terms-writings`). *lādaʿat kol-ʾanšê maʿăśēhû* 'that all the men of his making may know': the ASV supplies an object ('may know [it]'), and some revocalize *ʾanšê* to *ʾănāšîm*, 'that all people may know his work'. The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`).

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹ֣א חַיָּ֣ה בְמוֹ־אָ֑רֶב וּבִמְע֖וֹנֹתֶ֣יהָ תִשְׁכֹּֽן׃

i18n.en: Then the beast goes into its lair, and remains in its dens.

notes.official: *ḥayyâ* 'the beast' is the wild animal; *bĕmô-ʾāreb* 'into its lair'.

paragraphs.text: מִן־הַ֭חֶדֶר תָּב֣וֹא סוּפָ֑ה וּֽמִמְּזָרִ֥ים קָרָֽה׃

i18n.en: Out of the chamber comes the storm, and cold out of the north.

notes.official: *min-haḥeder tābôʾ sûpâ* 'Out of the chamber comes the storm' (the ASV supplies 'of the south'; the line does not). *sûpâ* 'storm' has one English word here and at Prov 10:25 (ASV 'whirlwind' there), and stays distinct from *sĕʿārâ* 'whirlwind' of 38:1 (central `min-ha-se-arah`). *ûmimmĕzārîm qārâ* 'and cold out of the north': *mĕzārîm* (hapax) is literally 'scatterers', usually taken as the scattering north winds (BDB; ASV 'the north'). A link with *mazzārôt* (38:32) is also proposed (Pope, AB 15).

paragraphs.text: מִנִּשְׁמַת־אֵ֥ל יִתֶּן־קָ֑רַח וְרֹ֖חַב מַ֣יִם בְּמוּצָֽק׃

i18n.en: By the breath of El ice is given, and the breadth of the waters is constrained.

notes.official: *minnišmat-ʾēl yitten-qāraḥ* 'By the breath of El ice is given': *nĕšāmâ* 'breath' (the central `neshamah-chayim` governs *nišmat ḥayyîm* only); *ʾēl* 'El' (`shaddai-eloah`). *wĕrōḥab mayim bĕmûṣāq* 'and the breadth of the waters is constrained': BDB derives *mûṣāq* here from *ṣwq* 'constrain' (cf. 36:16; ASV 'straitened'). NJPS takes it as *mûṣāq* 'cast metal', the word of v 18 ('The expanse of water becomes solid'). The line keeps the ASV sense and notes the possible echo of v 18.

paragraphs.text: אַף־בְּ֭רִי יַטְרִ֣יחַ עָ֑ב יָ֝פִ֗יץ עֲנַ֣ן אוֹרֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Also with moisture he loads the thick cloud; he scatters the cloud of his lightning.

notes.official: *ʾap-bĕrî yaṭrîaḥ ʿāb* 'Also with moisture he loads the thick cloud' (*rî*, hapax, 'moisture'); *yāpîṣ ʿănan ʾôrô* 'he scatters the cloud of his lightning'. *ʿāb* 'thick cloud' and *ʿānān* 'cloud' are kept apart, and both are distinct from *šĕḥāqîm* 'clouds' (vv 18, 21; central `shechaqim-clouds-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְה֤וּא מְסִבּ֨וֹת ׀ מִתְהַפֵּ֣ךְ בתחבולתו [בְּתַחְבּוּלֹתָ֣יו] לְפָעֳלָ֑ם כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְצַוֵּ֓ם ׀ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י תֵבֵ֣ל אָֽרְצָה׃

i18n.en: And it turns round and round by his guidance, to do whatever he commands them over the face of the inhabited world, on the earth —

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *btḥbwltw* (singular, 'by his guidance') / Qere *bĕtaḥbûlōtāyw* (plural, 'by his steerings', a nautical word). The Qere is translated, and English 'guidance' carries the plural collectively (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-writings`). *mĕsibbôt mithappēk* 'it turns round and round'; *ʿal-pĕnê tēbēl ʾārĕṣâ* 'over the face of the inhabited world, on the earth' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: אִם־לְשֵׁ֥בֶט אִם־לְאַרְצ֑וֹ אִם־לְ֝חֶ֗סֶד יַמְצִאֵֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: whether for a rod, or for his land, or for kindness, he causes it to come.

notes.official: *ʾim-lĕšēbeṭ ʾim-lĕʾarṣô ʾim-lĕḥesed yamṣiʾēhû* 'whether for a rod, or for his land, or for kindness, he causes it to come'. *lĕʾarṣô* 'for his land' (MT, ASV; central `eretz`) sits awkwardly between punishment and kindness, and commentators propose *lōʾ rāṣâ* 'for those he does not favour' or similar (Clines, WBC 18A). The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). *ḥesed* is 'kindness' under the central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness` (ASV 'lovingkindness').

paragraphs.text: הַאֲזִ֣ינָה זֹּ֣את אִיּ֑וֹב עֲ֝מֹ֗ד וְהִתְבּוֹנֵ֤ן ׀ נִפְלְא֬וֹת אֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Give ear to this, Job; stand still, and consider the wonders of El.

notes.official: *haʾăzînâ zōʾt ʾiyyôb* 'Give ear to this, Job' (English name form, as throughout job-woh); *niplĕʾôt ʾēl* 'the wonders of El' (`shaddai-eloah`).

paragraphs.text: הֲ֭תֵדַע בְּשׂוּם־אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝הוֹפִ֗יעַ א֣וֹר עֲנָנֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Do you know how Eloah lays his charge upon them, and makes the lightning of his cloud shine?

notes.official: *hătēdaʿ bĕśûm-ʾĕlôah ʿălêhem* 'Do you know how Eloah lays his charge upon them': *ʾĕlôah* 'Eloah' (central `shaddai-eloah`). *wĕhôpîaʿ ʾôr ʿănānô* 'and makes the lightning of his cloud shine'. Elihu's 'Do you know ...?' questions anticipate YHWH's in chapter 38 (38:33).

paragraphs.text: הֲ֭תֵדַע עַל־מִפְלְשֵׂי־עָ֑ב מִ֝פְלְא֗וֹת תְּמִ֣ים דֵּעִֽים׃

i18n.en: Do you know the balancings of the thick cloud, the wonders of the one who is perfect in knowledge —

notes.official: *mipleśê-ʿāb* 'the balancings of the thick cloud' (ASV; hapax, cf. *peles* 'balance'); *miplĕʾôt tĕmîm dēʿîm* 'the wonders of the one who is perfect in knowledge'. At 36:4 Elihu claimed *tĕmîm dēʿôt* for himself.

paragraphs.text: אֲשֶׁר־בְּגָדֶ֥יךָ חַמִּ֑ים בְּהַשְׁקִ֥ט אֶ֝֗רֶץ מִדָּרֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: you whose garments are warm when the earth is stilled by the south wind?

notes.official: *bĕhašqiṭ ʾereṣ middārôm* 'when the earth is stilled by the south wind': the hot, still air of the sirocco (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: תַּרְקִ֣יעַ עִ֭מּוֹ לִשְׁחָקִ֑ים חֲ֝זָקִ֗ים כִּרְאִ֥י מוּצָֽק׃

i18n.en: Can you, with him, spread out the clouds, strong as a molten mirror?

notes.official:
*tarqîaʿ ʿimmô lišḥāqîm ḥăzāqîm kirʾî mûṣāq* 'Can you, with him, spread out the clouds, strong as a molten mirror?' The verb *rqʿ* is 'beat out, hammer flat, spread out', the root of *rāqîaʿ* 'dome' (central `raqia`); the line keeps the ASV 'spread out' and records the root sense here. *šĕḥāqîm* is 'clouds' under the new central `shechaqim-clouds-cross-corpus`: the word means 'fine dust, cloud' (BDB; HALOT), the stable job-woh 38:37 already renders it 'clouds' ('Who can count the clouds in wisdom'), and a separate English word keeps it apart from *šāmayim* 'skies' (v 3). The ASV 'sky', NRSV 'skies' and NJPS 'heavens' are recorded. *ḥăzāqîm* 'strong' agrees with *šĕḥāqîm*; *kirʾî mûṣāq* 'like a mirror of cast metal', the polished bronze mirrors of antiquity (cf. Ex 38:8).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse in a French wording with 'des nuages, solides comme un miroir de métal fondu' ('clouds, solid as a mirror of molten metal'). It asks whether man is capable of making such 'solid clouds', in reality metallic flying craft, which people of that time thought impossible for any but God. The line's 'clouds' rests on the lexical entry above and the job-woh 38:37 precedent. *ḥăzāqîm* stays 'strong' (ASV), and the line makes no claim about what the clouds are. The canon's English edition has 'the sky, which is strong' ('hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass?'); the canon itself is therefore divided, and the line's 'clouds' follows the lexical entry, not either wording.

paragraphs.text: ה֭וֹדִיעֵנוּ מַה־נֹּ֣אמַר ל֑וֹ לֹ֥א־נַ֝עֲרֹ֗ךְ מִפְּנֵי־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

i18n.en: Teach us what we shall say to him; we cannot set things in order because of darkness.

notes.official: *hôdîʿēnû mah-nnōʾmar lô* 'Teach us what we shall say to him'; *lōʾ-naʿărōk mippĕnê-ḥōšek* 'we cannot set things in order because of darkness' (*ʿrk* 'arrange', also of setting out a legal case, 13:18; 23:4).

paragraphs.text: הַֽיְסֻפַּר־ל֭וֹ כִּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אִֽם־אָ֥מַר אִ֝֗ישׁ כִּ֣י יְבֻלָּֽע׃

i18n.en: Shall it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man say that he would be swallowed up?

notes.official: *hayĕsuppar-lô kî ʾădabbēr ʾim-ʾāmar ʾîš kî yĕbullāʿ* 'Shall it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man say that he would be swallowed up?' (ASV sense). The second half can also be construed as a condition ('If a man speaks, surely he will be swallowed up'); the ASV structure is kept as the more literal (Clines, WBC 18A, discusses both).

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֤ה ׀ לֹ֘א רָ֤אוּ א֗וֹר בָּהִ֣יר ה֭וּא בַּשְּׁחָקִ֑ים וְר֥וּחַ עָ֝בְרָ֗ה וַֽתְּטַהֲרֵֽם׃

i18n.en: And now they do not see the light — it is bright in the clouds — but a wind has passed and cleared them.

notes.official: *wĕʿattâ lōʾ rāʾû ʾôr bāhîr hûʾ baššĕḥāqîm wĕrûaḥ ʿābĕrâ wattĕṭahărēm* 'And now they do not see the light — it is bright in the clouds — but a wind has passed and cleared them'. *ʾôr* is here the sun's light, hidden in the cloud mass until the wind clears it. *šĕḥāqîm* is 'clouds' (central `shechaqim-clouds-cross-corpus`; ASV 'skies'), which also gives 'cleared them' its natural antecedent. *rûaḥ* is the wind (`ruach-wind-breath-spirit-writings`).

paragraphs.text: מִ֭צָּפוֹן זָהָ֣ב יֶֽאֱתֶ֑ה עַל־אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ נ֣וֹרָא הֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: Out of the north comes golden splendor; upon Eloah is fearsome majesty.

notes.official: *miṣṣāpôn zāhāb yeʾĕteh* 'Out of the north comes golden splendor' (ASV): literally 'gold', the brightness of the northern sky after the storm. Some see the gold of the northern divine mountain (cf. Ugaritic Ṣapānu; Isa 14:13). *ʿal-ʾĕlôah nôrāʾ hôd* 'upon Eloah is fearsome majesty' (`shaddai-eloah`).

paragraphs.text: שַׁדַּ֣י לֹֽא־מְ֭צָאנֻהוּ שַׂגִּיא־כֹ֑חַ וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט וְרֹב־צְ֝דָקָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְעַנֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: Shaddai — we cannot find him out; he is great in power, and in justice and abundant righteousness he will not afflict.

notes.official: *šadday lōʾ-mĕṣāʾnuhû* 'Shaddai — we cannot find him out': the name is kept (central `shaddai-eloah`; ASV 'the Almighty'). *śaggîʾ-kōaḥ* 'he is great in power'; *ûmišpāṭ wĕrōb-ṣĕdāqâ lōʾ yĕʿanneh* 'and in justice and abundant righteousness he will not afflict' (with another division, 'he does not violate justice').

paragraphs.text: לָ֭כֵן יְרֵא֣וּהוּ אֲנָשִׁ֑ים לֹֽא־יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה כָּל־חַכְמֵי־לֵֽב׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Therefore men fear him; he does not regard any who are wise of heart.

notes.official: *lākēn yĕrēʾûhû ʾănāšîm* 'Therefore men fear him'; *lōʾ-yirʾeh kol-ḥakmê-lēb* 'he does not regard any who are wise of heart' (ASV). The petucha (פ) closing Elihu's speech is kept in the Hebrew text.
